BiblicalUsage: Ke-eb means pain, sorrow, suffering of body or mind: Job 2:13 says his friends sat with him seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word, for they saw that his grief was very great. Psalms 39:2 says, I was dumb with silence, I held my peace, even from good, and my sorrow was stirred. Isaiah 17:11 says the harvest shall be a heap in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow. Jeremiah 15:18 cries, why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed?
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sorrow is the one language every sufferer speaks: Job's friends knew to sit silent, David knew to hold his peace, and Jeremiah asked God why the pain would not end. I hold that God hears the question even when the wound refuses to heal.
